assets.prompt: full-bleed single portrait illustration, not a picture printed on a book page, no paper border, no page margin, no book edge. 1844 Nottinghamshire, England, inside a dim textile mill at night. Several textile workers have rushed into the factory and are smashing a newly installed mechanical loom. Do not portray them as criminals; portray them as exhausted, frightened, angry craftsmen whose lifelong hand skills are being displaced. Rough cloth shirts, dusty hands, old hammers and hand tools, scattered thread spools, broken wood pieces, heavy iron loom machinery. The loom should feel huge, cold, and historically early-industrial, with moonlight through a tall factory window and warm oil-lamp light in the room. The composition should express a historical time lag: technology has changed, but the workers' skills, income, dignity, and identity have not yet found a new support system. Watercolor texture, visible paper grain in the paint only, restrained ink linework, deep sea-blue shadows, moonlit silver, warm gold oil-lamp glow, graphite gray, a very subtle cyan glint as a quiet future-technology metaphor, not science fiction. Serious philosophical book illustration, historical and human, moderate breathing space. No text, no letters, no numbers, no Chinese characters, no pseudo text, no watermark, no robot, no modern hard hats, no modern factory, no guns, no gore, no comic exaggeration, no movie poster look, no plastic 3D, no book page, no page border, no open book, no page spine, no fold crease.
